# Execution Requirements Quality Checklist: Execution Model and History

**Purpose**: Review whether Feature 006 execution lifecycle, snapshot, history, API, and UX requirements are complete, clear, consistent, and objectively assessable.
**Created**: 2026-09-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are manual-execution eligibility conditions explicitly separated from Monitoring Configuration and schedule enabled states? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the specification reconcile the required initial `pending` state with the same request's `pending → running → completed` orchestration outcome and API response state? [Clarity, Conflict, Spec §FR-002, §FR-022, §SC-001, Plan §API and read semantics]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the one-active-execution rule and the expected outcome for overlapping requests defined independently of frontend button state? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004–FR-005, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK004 Are all configuration and scope values required in the immutable snapshot identified, including how empty selections and group-level intent are represented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007–FR-008, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK005 Are lifecycle timestamp and counter ownership rules complete for creation, each transition, and final states? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013–FR-014, §FR-022–FR-023]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the requirements for global and per-configuration history, filtering, ordering, pagination, and retired-configuration access sufficiently complete for a growing history? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016–FR-018, Plan §API and read semantics]

## Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [ ] CHK007 Is “completed” consistently defined as successful Feature 006 orchestration without implying repository mining across the spec, API contract, and frontend terminology? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §FR-023, §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Are allowed transitions, terminal states, invalid transition outcomes, and the meaning of “set once” unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011–FR-013]
- [ ] CHK009 Are conflict outcomes clear for both an already-active execution and two overlapping requests, including whether each rejected request preserves existing history? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004–FR-005, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK010 Is idempotency behavior for an uncertain response after the fast orchestration-only completion explicitly included in requirements, including same-key replay and key reuse with different request intent? [Gap, Dependency, Constitution Principle VII, Plan §Idempotency]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the public snapshot projection and internal snapshot requirements clearly distinguished, especially for scope fingerprints, snapshot schema version, and credential metadata? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-009, Plan §Snapshot and persistence]
- [ ] CHK012 Are “safe error summary” and normalized error outcomes defined clearly enough to distinguish allowed user-facing summaries from prohibited exception, database, provider, and secret details? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, Plan §API and read semantics]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are disabled-but-not-retired, retired, missing, and already-active configuration cases distinguished with clear eligibility outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001, §FR-006, §FR-021, §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK014 Are configuration edits, scope changes, credential changes, retirement, and removal all covered by explicit historical snapshot retention expectations? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK015 Are empty scope, selected groups, selected repositories, and mixed group/repository scope all covered without implying descendant expansion? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-007–FR-009]
- [ ] CHK016 Are persistence failure and unexpected orchestration failure outcomes specified so the requirements do not permit a misleading active execution or unsafe error detail? [Gap, Recovery, Spec §FR-015, §FR-022–FR-023, Plan §Aggregate and lifecycle]
- [ ] CHK017 Are repeated manual requests after a completed execution distinguished from retries of the original uncertain request? [Clarity, Edge Case, Constitution Principle VII, Plan §Idempotency]

## Acceptance Criteria and Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK018 Can the concurrent-request success/conflict criterion be measured deterministically, including the boundary between overlapping requests and a new request after completion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §FR-004–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK019 Are UTC timestamp semantics and the reference-clock expectations explicit in the requirements, not only in implementation design? [Gap, Consistency, Spec §FR-013, Plan §Aggregate and lifecycle]
- [ ] CHK020 Are accessibility requirements explicit for manual execution, conflict/loading feedback, history navigation, status labels, and execution detail headings? [Gap, Accessibility, Constitution Principle XI, Spec §FR-018–FR-019]
- [ ] CHK021 Are response-size or history-retention expectations sufficiently defined to support bounded global history without contradicting the API's pagination contract? [Clarity, Non-Functional, Spec §FR-016–FR-017, API Contract §Global listing]

## Dependencies and Scope Boundaries

- [ ] CHK022 Are Feature 008/009 responsibilities clearly separated from Feature 006, particularly repository processing while running and scheduled-trigger creation? [Consistency, Dependency, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions, Scope Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK023 Are configuration retirement and physical deletion semantics aligned with Feature 002 so retaining execution history does not imply a new configuration lifecycle? [Consistency, Dependency, Spec §FR-020–FR-021, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK024 Are public API status mutation, credential access, GitLab discovery, repository cloning, findings, and dashboard analytics explicitly excluded? [Scope, Spec §FR-009, §FR-024, Scope Boundaries]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after the reviewer determines that the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- This checklist evaluates requirements quality, not implementation behavior.
